A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CTE research despite the changed title and expanded scope. Text, equations, figures and tables support comparison throughout. v1 ends after its references; v2 includes supplementary Sections 8–12, which were also inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original microscopy segmentation-ranking experiments, quantitative correlations in Tables 1–2, and perturbation analyses in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2 reports original microscopy, classification, ToothFairy2, post-adaptation and public-model ranking results, with additional experiments and failure examples in the supplement.

M1.justification: The perturb-and-compare estimator, median aggregation and core consistency measures remain. v2 adds weighted per-class aggregation for multiclass segmentation and dropout across all layers or bottleneck-plus-skip connections, extending v1's bottleneck perturbation (Sections 3.3–3.4; supplementary Section 10). CTE-VRand becomes CTE-ARS with the same formula.

E1.justification: v2 adds 42-class 3D ToothFairy2 CBCT segmentation, Covid-IF cell segmentation and mitochondria patch classification. Within retained nuclei coverage, SBIAD634 is removed from semantic target evaluation and DSB2018 from instance target evaluation; both datasets remain elsewhere. These changes are supported by v1 Figure 2 and v2 Sections 4.1 and 8.

E2.justification: v1 quantitatively compares CTE only with CCFV. v2 Table 1 retains CCFV and adds NLEEP, GBC, Hscore, LEEP, LogME, NCTI, Regularised-Hscore and Transfer Score. Transfer Score also provides a post-UDA comparator in Table 3. Both versions report no alternative ranking baseline for instance segmentation.

E3.justification: The evaluation moves beyond predominantly U-Net model banks to diverse architectures and models trained with and without augmentation. Reported mitochondria candidate counts increase from 3 to 15 and cell counts from 5 to 8. Cell evaluation changes from 256-by-256 tiles to full z-slices. Added experiments introduce classification, multiclass CBCT, Mean Teacher/AdaBN adaptation and supervised fine-tuning protocols. The three correlation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v1 already tests input versus feature perturbations, hard versus soft consistency and dropout strength. v2 substantially extends sensitivity analyses across perturbation types, strengths and placements. It adds classification-versus-segmentation diagnostics, checks baseline rankings against final supervised fine-tuning, and investigates stable-but-incorrect predictions and cell/nucleus confusion (Figure 2, Table 25, supplementary Sections 11–12 and Figures 5–6).

E5.justification: v2 adds correlation p-values and significance indicators at 0.05 and 0.01 in Tables 2–3 and supplementary tables. Across-dataset means and standard deviations were already reported in v1. Both retain a single perturbed pass plus an unperturbed pass; no new seed-based replication or confidence-interval procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Microscopy summaries are replaced under revised settings: for example, Table 1 reports mitochondria CTE-NHD feature Kendall correlation of 1.00 with 3 candidates in v1 and 0.69 with 15 in v2. These are not comparable fixed-protocol performance estimates. New findings include ToothFairy2 overall Kendall and Spearman correlations of 1.00 for gamma-based CTE-NHD, post-UDA results, public-model rankings and extensive perturbation results. v2 also reports strong supervised LEEP performance absent from v1's comparisons.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.3 extends the consistency-score definition from foreground-restricted calculation to weighted per-class aggregation for multiclass masks. Otherwise, the core EI, NHD, Rand-score and perturbation mathematics remain equivalent, and the same-task transfer assumption persists. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs; v2's expanded margin discussion is conceptual motivation.

C1.justification: The original source-free, unsupervised ranking and two-pass efficiency claims remain. v2 broadens the main contribution from zero-shot microscopy ranking to multiclass biomedical challenge models and post-UDA selection. Its introduction also makes the failure of most classification-derived ranking methods on biomedical segmentation a prominent scientific claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds decision-boundary and feature-geometry explanations, including why LEEP behaves differently from embedding-based baselines. It revises v1's preference for hard consistency and feature perturbations toward broadly comparable performance. New limitations address collapsed predictions, consistently wrong structures after adaptation, cell/nucleus task confusion, residual connections and poor alignment with boundary-sensitive metrics (Sections 3.2, 5–6 and supplementary Sections 10 and 12.4).

D1.justification: Compared with v1's brief setup, v2 supplies dataset-specific split counts and volume identifiers, resampling and patch-processing instructions, perturbation ranges, instance postprocessing, GPU specifications and CUDA/PyTorch versions. It explains nnU-Net planning and public models' instantiation procedures. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation. Code release is newly promised on acceptance, but availability is not established.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands research positioning through a dedicated Related Work section covering supervised transfer metrics, unsupervised adaptation validation, generalisation and uncertainty estimation. Added literature includes Transfer Score, LogME, NCTI, adaptation methods and generalist biomedical segmenters. It explicitly challenges the proposed extension of classification ranking methods to segmentation, beyond v1's brief introductory positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the paper gains dedicated Related Work, Motivation, Experimental Setting and Limitations sections plus a structured supplement. The methods narrative is reordered and expanded. The title, author list and Rand-score terminology also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the overview, replaces the original correlation panels with classification comparisons and illustrated model-ranking case studies, and presents expanded sensitivity evidence in supplementary tables. Summary tables are substantially restructured, with new dental and UDA tables, supplementary Tables 5–33 and failure-example Figures 5–6.

improvement.justification: v1's broad claims relied on small, mostly U-Net banks and one supervised comparator. v2 substantially strengthens validation through diverse architectures, supervised and unsupervised baselines, and experiments testing classification-versus-segmentation and fine-tuning explanations. Detailed reproducibility information and explicit stable-but-wrong failure cases make applicability much easier to assess. Some reporting inconsistencies remain, including nuclei model counts in Tables 1 and 20, and code is only promised, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and interpretability.
